prompt: What does a diffusion model learn to do?

choices.text: Retrieve the stored training picture closest to the prompt
choices.why: Nothing is copied from storage; it learned what pictures look like at every level of noise.

choices.text: Paint a picture stroke by stroke in the order an artist would
choices.why: It removes noise from the whole picture at once, step by step.

choices.text: Predict the noise in a noisy picture
choices.why: Right. Subtracting the prediction gives a slightly cleaner picture, step after step.

choices.text: Translate the prompt into pixels word by word
choices.why: The prompt nudges each denoising step; words do not map to pixels.

prompt: In noise.py, at which of the printed steps did Tesseract last read the title?
At step 400, how much of the picture was left, in percent?
What does raising guidance do?

choices.text: Adds more denoising steps to every run
choices.why: The number of steps is a separate setting.

choices.text: Fixes the seed so runs repeat
choices.why: The seed is the starting noise, not a scale.

choices.text: Raises the resolution of the output
choices.why: The size is fixed by what the model was trained for.

choices.text: Follows the prompt more literally
choices.why: Right, with less varied pictures: the difference between the step with and without the prompt is scaled up.

prompt: With OpenAI's Images API, how do you see how much one prompt varies?

choices.text: Fix the seed and change it by one
choices.why: That API exposes no seed.

choices.text: Ask for several pictures with n and look at all of them
choices.why: Right. One picture of a prompt is not a measurement of it.

choices.text: Lower the guidance to zero
choices.why: That changes the model's behaviour, not your view of its spread.

choices.text: Send the same request until the picture stops changing
choices.why: It will not stop changing: each run starts from new noise.

prompt: Why is an image prompt closer to a caption than to an instruction?

choices.text: It learned from pictures and their captions
choices.why: Right. A description of a picture matches what it saw.

choices.text: Because image models cannot read verbs
choices.why: They read verbs; the point is what they were trained on.

choices.text: Because captions are shorter, and short prompts work better
choices.why: Length is not the reason; the composition line is long and essential.

choices.text: Because instructions are refused by the provider's policy
choices.why: Policies refuse content, not grammatical forms.

prompt: Match each part of the banner prompt to what it controls.

pairs.right: what it seems to be made with

prompt: Why does the banner's composition line matter more than the others?

choices.text: It is the longest line
choices.why: Length is not importance.

choices.text: It holds the banner's real requirement
choices.why: Right: room on the right for the headline. Without it the picture is unusable, however good it looks.

choices.text: Models read composition first
choices.why: Order matters for truncation, but that is not why this line decides.

choices.text: It names the style the shop is known for
choices.why: Style is the medium and palette lines.

prompt: A prompt says "no people". What is the problem?

choices.text: Providers refuse prompts that mention people
choices.why: They refuse real people, not the word.

choices.text: Negation makes the prompt longer than 77 tokens
choices.why: Two words do not reach that ceiling.

choices.text: Nothing; it is the recommended way to exclude something
choices.why: The section recommends the opposite.

choices.text: It names exactly what should be absent
choices.why: Right. Describe a scene where people are out of place instead, or use a negative prompt where one exists.

prompt: The CLIP text encoder reads ___ tokens of a prompt and ignores the rest.
Why change one part of a prompt at a time?

choices.text: Because the API refuses two changes in one request
choices.why: The API knows nothing about your changes; it sees one prompt.

choices.text: Because shorter changes cost fewer tokens
choices.why: Image generation is priced per picture here.

choices.text: To keep the prompt under 77 tokens
choices.why: Length is a separate concern.

choices.text: So you know which change caused what you see
choices.why: Right. Two at once and you cannot tell which one did it.

prompt: How many prompts did axes.py write to grid.json?
What came back from the course's images_server.py?

choices.text: Watercolour pictures of books
choices.why: No image model runs in this course; the server is a stand-in.

choices.text: An error, because no model runs
choices.why: The API answered normally, with cards.

choices.text: Cards saying no model drew them, at the size asked
choices.why: Right. The request, the log and the files are real; the drawing is not.

choices.text: The same picture for every prompt
choices.why: Each card carries its own prompt written on it.

prompt: Which columns does the lesson say to add to the log when running against a real model? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: The model and its version
choices.why: Right. Next quarter's model is a different experiment.

choices.text: The seed, where exposed
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Whether the picture met the requirement
choices.why: Right. That column turns a folder into a decision.

choices.text: The file size in bytes
choices.why: The stand-in's log records it, but it decides nothing about the picture.

prompt: What is the cheapest way to keep fifty banners looking alike?

choices.text: Use the same seed every week
choices.why: The same seed with a different subject is a different picture; and the API has none.

choices.text: Name a well-known illustrator
choices.why: That copies a person's work, and providers refuse or soften it.

choices.text: Generate all fifty at once in one request
choices.why: Batch size does not hold a look across weeks of different subjects.

choices.text: Keep the medium, style and palette parts fixed
choices.why: Right. Only the subject changes week to week.

prompt: A banner is right except for one cup on the table. What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Edit it with a mask over the cup
choices.why: Right, with a prompt for what goes there. The rest of the picture is kept.

choices.text: Generate again with "no cup" in the prompt
choices.why: That starts from new noise and loses what was right, and puts cup in the prompt.

choices.text: Raise guidance and generate again
choices.why: Still a new run from new noise.

choices.text: Crop the cup out
choices.why: That breaks the composition the banner needs.

prompt: Why avoid "in the style of" a living illustrator for a product?

choices.text: Models do not know the names of any illustrators
choices.why: They often do, which is the problem.

choices.text: It makes the prompt too long for the text encoder
choices.why: A name is a few tokens.

choices.text: It copies a person's work without consent
choices.why: Right. The work is identifiable and the person is not paid; describe the qualities you want instead.

choices.text: It lowers the resolution
choices.why: Style words do not change the size.

prompt: Why do generators get counts wrong, as in five books coming back as four?

choices.text: The prompt was cut at 77 tokens
choices.why: Five is near the start of the prompt.

choices.text: Providers refuse exact numbers
choices.why: No policy refuses a count.

choices.text: The seed decides the number of objects
choices.why: The seed is starting noise; it does not hold a count.

choices.text: The model learned what a stack looks like, not how to count
choices.why: Right. Precision about numbers was rare in what it learned.

prompt: The section says a generator's default person is a statistical average. What follows for a shop?

choices.text: Decide who appears and say so in the prompt
choices.why: Right. Leaving it to the default is also a decision.

choices.text: Nothing, since the model chose it
choices.why: Publishing it makes it the shop's choice.

choices.text: People must never appear in generated pictures
choices.why: The section says to decide who they are, not to ban them.

choices.text: Use a higher guidance so the average is avoided
choices.why: Guidance follows the prompt more literally; it does not change what the default is.

prompt: Why may Marginalia draw a cover of Dom Casmurro but not copy a publisher's cover of it?

choices.text: Generated pictures cannot infringe anything
choices.why: Generated or not, a copy of someone's work is a copy.

choices.text: Because the lab drew it, not a model, so no rule applies
choices.why: Who drew it is not what makes it allowed.

choices.text: The novel is public domain; that cover design is not
choices.why: Right. The text is free; someone's design of a cover is their property.

choices.text: Book covers are never protected
choices.why: A designed cover is someone's work.

prompt: What happened to the PNG's Source note after stamp.py resized the picture?

choices.text: It was kept, because Pillow copies metadata
choices.why: The second line printed an empty dictionary.

choices.text: It was lost: the edited file had no text
choices.why: Right. Nothing asked Pillow to copy it.

choices.text: It moved into the pixels as a watermark
choices.why: A text chunk is not a watermark; it was simply dropped.

choices.text: It was rewritten with the new size
choices.why: The edited file had no text at all.

prompt: Which marking is meant to survive a screenshot of the picture?

choices.text: A watermark in the pixels, such as SynthID
choices.why: Right. It lives in the picture itself.

choices.text: A C2PA record in the metadata
choices.why: A screenshot is a new file; the metadata stays behind.

choices.text: A text chunk saying where it came from
choices.why: One resize was enough to lose it.

choices.text: The file name
choices.why: A screenshot has a new name.

prompt: Which of Marginalia's three practices depends on no file surviving?

choices.text: Copying metadata across when resizing
choices.why: That is about the file surviving.

choices.text: Keeping the provider's C2PA record
choices.why: That lives in the file.

choices.text: Reading the published file to check
choices.why: That checks the file.

choices.text: A visible line under the banner
choices.why: Right. It costs nothing and needs no file.

prompt: Why write the judging list before the first picture arrives?

choices.text: Because the API needs it in the request
choices.why: The list is for the person, not the API.

choices.text: To shorten the prompt
choices.why: It does not touch the prompt.

choices.text: Because generators read the list and follow it
choices.why: The list is never sent to the generator.

choices.text: So a striking miss is still rejected
choices.why: Right. A picture that misses the requirement is a miss however good it looks; otherwise the judging turns into taste.

prompt: At 0.039 dollars a picture, what does one accepted banner cost if one picture in four passes the list?
After two rounds, the watercolour banners all have a mug drawn in the empty right third. What is the next experiment?

choices.text: Change the medium and the palette together, to get away from the café look
choices.why: Two changes at once, and neither is the part that is failing.

choices.text: Add "no mug" to the prompt
choices.why: That puts mug into the prompt.

choices.text: Vary only the subject or composition part, such as dropping the café
choices.why: Right. The café table invites a cup; vary the part that causes it, one at a time.

choices.text: Generate ten more of the same prompt until one has no mug
choices.why: Possible, and expensive per accepted picture; it does not fix the cause.
